content.text:
No. This repo doesn't document how to set up the ArgoCD CLI. It doesn't explain installing it or logging in to the server, and it doesn't configure server, context or token variables. `mise.toml` doesn't pin it as a tool either. I also checked `../mothership-gitops` and it has nothing on this.

The CLI only shows up as one command, `argocd app sync argocd-ha`, in two places. It isn't the only option in either:

- `scripts/README.md:103` gives it next to the `kubectl patch` option.
- `docs/plans/gitops-bootstrap-hybrid.md:211` is the bootstrap plan. It says "UI or CLI".

Everything else uses `kubectl` against the `argocd` namespace. That includes `scripts/disaster-recovery.sh`, which prints a `kubectl -n argocd patch application argocd-ha ...` command for the manual HA sync. The only thing these docs need the CLI for is that one manual sync, and kubectl already covers it.

ArgoCD lives in `mothership-gitops` (`OPERATIONS.md` and `DEPLOYMENT.md` point there), so CLI setup docs would fit better in that repo. Doing it here would mean pinning `argocd` in `mise.toml` and adding a login note. The plan says the server runs with `--insecure` and Tailscale handles TLS, so that note would cover `argocd login <tailscale-host> --grpc-web` and Infisical for the admin password. I can draft it in either repo if you want.
it's managed by homebrew. but noted, mothership-gitops is the proper repo for it

Understood. So the setup note in `mothership-gitops` would need just two parts: install with `brew install argocd`, kept out of `mise.toml`, and a login section for the Tailscale-fronted server.

Nothing needs to change in Omni-Scale. The `argocd app sync argocd-ha` references in `scripts/README.md` and the bootstrap plan already give the `kubectl` option alongside it or the UI.

If you want, I can draft that section in `mothership-gitops`. Before I do, I'd check its existing docs for where it fits and confirm the ArgoCD server's Tailscale hostname.

I fixed the warning in `mise.toml` by moving the deprecated setting under the new `task` key:

```toml
[settings.task]
run_auto_install = true
```

On mise 2026.11.3, `mise settings get task.run_auto_install` returns `true` and `mise tasks ls` runs with no deprecation warning.

The file still declares `min_version = "2024.9.5"`, and mise versions that old probably don't recognise `task.run_auto_install`. If anything runs this repo on an older mise, raise `min_version` to whichever release added the new key. If everything is on the current version, it doesn't matter.

min_version
A plain string is a hard minimum. Older mise releases stop with an error and print upgrade instructions:

1
min_version = "2026.1.0"


Add a soft minimum to warn without failing:

1
min_version = { hard = "2025.6.0", soft = "2026.1.0" }


Set hard to the oldest release that understands this file and soft to the release you want teammates on. { soft = "2026.1.0" } on its own is also valid.

min_version = { hard = "2026.2.17", soft = "2026.11.3" }

- **Soft minimum, `2026.11.3`:** this is just the version you have installed now, so older installs get a warning but still work. Lower it if you'd rather not nag about anything older.
